question.problem: Given that $X∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.7)$ and $Y∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.4)$ are independent, calculate $P(X=1\,\cup \,Y=0).$
question.worked_solution:
By the addition law, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=1\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=1)+P(Y=0)-P(X=1\,\cap \,Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the multiplication law for independent events, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=1\,\cap \,Y=0) & =P(X=1)\cdot P(Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=1\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=1)+P(Y=0)-P(X=1)\cdot P(Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $X∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.7),$ we have

$$
P(X=1)=0.7,\,P(X=0)=0.3,
$$

and since $Y∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.4),$ we have

$$
P(Y=1)=0.4,\,P(Y=0)=0.6.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=1\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=1)+P(Y=0)-P(X=1)\cdot P(Y=0) \\  & =0.7+0.6-0.7\cdot 0.6 \\  & =1.3-0.42 \\  & =0.88.\end{aligned}
$$
